subsystems.name: Superconducting electrodes
subsystems.role: supply Cooper pairs to the weak link and set the phase difference across it.

subsystems.name: Semiconductor weak link
subsystems.role: the narrow channel where Andreev bound states form; strong spin–orbit coupling and a large g-factor make its states tunable by gate and by magnetic field.
parts: indium arsenide nanowire or quantum well
epitaxial aluminium shell with an uncoated gap

subsystems.name: Gate electrodes
subsystems.role: electrostatically tune how many conduction channels bridge the junction and how transparent they are.

subsystems.name: Microwave control and readout
subsystems.role: drives the transition between the two qubit levels and reports the state without destroying it.

subsystems.name: Cryogenic environment
subsystems.role: keeps the metal superconducting and the thermal population of the qubit levels negligible.

buildSteps.title: Grow the hybrid crystal
buildSteps.detail: Indium arsenide nanowires are grown by a catalytic vapour–liquid–solid process, or an indium arsenide quantum well is grown on a lattice-matched substrate; aluminium is then deposited in the same vacuum so the metal–semiconductor interface never oxidises.

buildSteps.title: Form the weak link
buildSteps.detail: Using shadowed evaporation or a stencil, the aluminium is interrupted along the wire to leave an uncoated semiconductor channel tens to a couple of hundred nanometres long — the junction where the Andreev levels will live.

buildSteps.title: Place the junction in a circuit
buildSteps.detail: The junction is embedded in a superconducting loop so that magnetic flux sets the phase difference across it, and local gates are deposited on a thin dielectric to tune the channel.

buildSteps.title: Add the readout resonator
buildSteps.detail: A low-loss superconducting microwave resonator is fabricated nearby and coupled to the junction so that its state shifts the resonator frequency, enabling dispersive readout.

buildSteps.title: Cool and characterise the junction
buildSteps.detail: The chip goes into a dilution refrigerator at roughly 10 millikelvin with heavy filtering; the switching current is measured against gate voltage and flux to find a regime with a few highly transparent channels.

buildSteps.title: Spectroscopically map the levels
buildSteps.detail: Microwaves are swept in frequency while phase and gate voltage are varied, revealing the discrete Andreev levels and their avoided crossings.

buildSteps.title: Drive coherently
buildSteps.detail: A chosen pair of levels is driven to produce Rabi oscillations, and energy relaxation and dephasing times are measured.

buildSteps.title: Measure the noise and parity environment
buildSteps.detail: Parity lifetime and sensitivity to charge offset are quantified — the whole point is that the state should ignore charge noise while remaining vulnerable to quasiparticles breaking Cooper pairs.

buildSteps.title: Couple two qubits
buildSteps.detail: Two junctions are linked through a shared resonator or coupler to attempt a two-qubit gate, the step that turns single devices into a modality.

prerequisites.why: clean, oxide-free aluminium on indium arsenide is what gives the junction its high transparency and reproducible levels.
dilution refrigerators, low-noise amplifiers and dispersive readout techniques were developed for conventional superconducting qubits and are reused directly.
stray quasiparticles flip the parity of the state and destroy coherence; shielding and gap engineering help but parity lifetimes are still short.
a qubit needs a clean, well-separated pair of levels, and device-to-device variability in nanowire junctions remains a real obstacle.
no entanglement between two Andreev bound state qubits has been established, so the scaling path is unproven.

pathway.milestone: coherent single-qubit operation of Andreev level and Andreev spin qubits in individual junctions, in a handful of university laboratories
pathway.unlocks: proof that superconductor–semiconductor hybrids can be more than a platform for exotic physics.

pathway.milestone: millisecond-scale parity and coherence lifetimes with reproducible, gate-tunable junctions
pathway.unlocks: serious comparison with conventional superconducting and spin qubits.

pathway.milestone: two-qubit gates and entanglement between hybrid qubits
pathway.unlocks: a genuine modality rather than a single-device demonstration.

pathway.milestone: small processors or hybrid elements integrated with standard superconducting circuits
pathway.unlocks: a realistic niche: compact, gate-tunable, charge-noise-tolerant qubits that borrow the wiring, resonators and control stack of the superconducting qubit industry.
